vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vikunja-task-api
Version: 2.4.0

The vikunja-task-api skill bundle is a legitimate integration for the Vikunja task management system. It provides a functional bash helper script (vikunja.sh) and comprehensive documentation (SKILL.md) for managing projects, tasks, and labels via the Vikunja API. The code uses standard environment variables for authentication, implements proper error handling, and contains no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose: it provides a Vikunja v2 API helper using curl/jq and requests only the Vikunja URL and token (or username/password) needed to operate.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required binaries (curl, jq), and declared envs (VIKUNJA_URL, primary VIKUNJA_TOKEN with username/password fallback) align with a Vikunja API integration. The included helper script implements the documented endpoints and actions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and vikunja.sh instruct the agent to read the skill file and environment variables and to call Vikunja endpoints. This is expected for an API integration. Minor note: the README tells the user to store credentials at ~/.openclaw/workspace/secure/api-fillin.env — this is guidance (not a hidden path requirement) but users should ensure that file is kept secure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are present (instruction-only plus an included shell helper). No URLs or archive downloads that would write arbitrary code to disk are used by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested secrets (VIKUNJA_TOKEN or VIKUNJA_USERNAME/VIKUNJA_PASSWORD) and VIKUNJA_URL are appropriate for the stated functionality. Minor inconsistency: the primary credential is VIKUNJA_TOKEN but SKILL.md and metadata allow token to be optional (username/password fallback) — this is reasonable but worth noting so users understand one of these credentials will be required to operate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request system-wide changes or modify other skills. The agent can be invoked autonomously (platform default), so the skill could perform API actions when used by an autonomous agent — expected for a task-management integration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: it will use curl + jq and your VIKUNJA_TOKEN (or username/password) to call your Vikunja server and can create, update, or delete tasks/projects. Before installing: 1) Use a dedicated API token with limited scope if possible and store it in a secure, non-world-readable file; 2) Confirm VIKUNJA_URL points to your trusted server (mistyped URL could send tokens elsewhere); 3) Be aware that an agent with access to this token can modify/delete data in Vikunja — revoke the token if you see unexpected activity; 4) Review the included vikunja.sh if you plan to run it locally (it only calls the Vikunja API and uses jq). If you do not want the agent to act autonomously on your tasks, avoid granting long-lived tokens or restrict agent permissions.
